summary.intent: Determine whether phase 73 of the CipherBox project had unresolved discussion points, then run /gsd-plan-phase to plan it — ensuring the correct feature branch (not the default docs/plan-phase-N branch) was used and that any tangentially-related pending todos got folded into scope.
summary.outcome: Phase 73 was planned end-to-end: 2 pending todos were folded into ROADMAP, the correct branch `feat/shared-write-navigation-correctness-web` was created and held throughout, research uncovered that SC4 (write-access refresh) was deeper than its source todo implied, 9 PLAN.md files were produced across 3 waves, plan-checker found 2 blockers + 1 warning (all fixed and re-verified to PASS), and STATE.md was advanced to reflect phase 73 as planned.

repo: GSD's `phase_branch_template` is `feat/{slug}`; correct branch names come from the phase directory slug minus the number (e.g. phase 72 → `feat/sdk-write-plane-durability-and-correctness`), not from letting the planner auto-generate one.
gsd-core plan-phase workflow Step 0 explicitly forbids creating/renaming/switching git branches during plan-phase — branch setup must happen before invoking the skill.

In useSharedWriteOps.ts, `runWithFailureUx` is never called at all — a real API 410 currently surfaces as an uncaught AxiosError instead of the expected tombstone UX (found during phase 73 research for SC4).
fetchShareKeys must be preserved when removing dead write-share key paths — only the dead folder-IPNS branch should be deleted, not the whole function (SC7 landmine).
Phase 73 SC sequencing was locked by research as SC7→SC6→SC1+SC2→SC4 due to dependency ordering between the seams touched.
Intel's API-SURFACE.md regeneration for phase 73 came back empty (0 symbols, HINT-only) — real grounding for planning had to come from RESEARCH.md/PATTERNS.md instead.

code.finding: TDD RED-task verify command piped through `grep ... || true`, masking the real exit code so the 'confirm RED' gate could never fail; fixed to invert on the test's actual exit code.
Same grep-masking anti-pattern as 73-02-PLAN.md in a parallel RED-task verify command; fixed identically.
Frontmatter `depends_on: [73-07, 73-01]` was missing an implied dependency on 73-05 for item-4 ordering; added without changing the plan's wave (stayed wave 3).

workflow: When classifying many pending todos (51) against a phase's scope, delegate the read-and-classify pass to a subagent rather than reading each todo directly, to conserve context.
When a plan-checker gate returns small, mechanical, fully-specified fixes (not judgment calls), apply them directly and re-run the checker rather than burning a full planner iteration.
Before committing agent-modified ROADMAP.md, diff it explicitly to guard against the known gsd-planner ROADMAP-truncation failure mode rather than trusting the agent's edit.
Sanity-check STATE.md's cursor position before treating it as ground truth — it can go stale (still showed phase 72 'verifying' after phase 72 had already merged to main).

friction: STATE.md had drifted from actual repo state (still marked Phase 72 as 'verifying' despite PR #602 already merged to main), requiring a manual cursor correction that was out of scope for the original task.

No `73-*` phase directory or discussion artifacts existed yet for phase 73, requiring several exploratory reads (ROADMAP, STATE, source todos) just to confirm there was nothing blocking before planning could start.
open_items: Phase 72 formal completion/closure in STATE.md's progress counters was left untouched (only the cursor was advanced) — still needs to be marked complete separately.
3 adjacent-but-separate pending todos (SDK merge parity, dead SDK scaffolding retirement, ESLint boundary rule) were deliberately left out of phase 73 scope; revisit if they become relevant.

Q1 from Phase 68 (co-writer offline during write-key rotation — explicit re-fetch vs. grace/notification) remains open and is related to phase 73's SC4 decision to wire the write-access refresh end-to-end.
